question: Five cards are lying on a table. Each card has a letter on one side and a whole number on the other side. The visible faces show \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(6.\) Jane said, “If a vowel is on one side of any card, then an even number is on the other side.” Mary showed Jane was wrong by turning over one card. Which card did Mary turn over?
solution:
To show Jane's statement is false, Mary needs a card with a vowel on one side and an odd number on the other.

The cards showing \(P\) and \(Q\) have consonants, so no number on their other sides can produce that counterexample. The cards showing \(4\) and \(6\) already have even numbers, so neither can violate the rule, whatever letter is hidden.

Only the card showing \(3\) can have an odd number paired with a vowel. Since Mary did disprove the statement, she must have turned over that card and found a vowel. The answer is \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
